ResStock 2025 Release 1 Measure Documentation: Advanced Air Sealing with Drill-and-Fill Wall Insulation Accessing Results This documentation covers the “Advanced Air Sealing with Drill-and-Fill Wall Insulation” measure upgrade methodology and briefly discusses key results. All results are available on the ResStock Open Energy Data Initiative “End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock” data lake and on the Data Viewer at resstock.nlr.gov. Measure Summary Measure Title Advanced Air Sealing with Drill-and-Fill Wall Insulation Measure This upgrade measure applies R-13 drill-and-fill insulation to exterior wood-stud walls Definition and is modeled with advanced air sealing. Advanced air sealing details are available in the measure documentation (Phoung, Lou and White 2025). Applicability The insulation portion of this measure applies to all dwellings with: • Uninsulated above-grade wood stud walls separating conditioned from unconditioned space. With these applicability constraints, this portion of the measure upgrade applies to about 30% of existing dwelling units. The advanced air sealing portion of the measure applies to dwelling units with infiltration rates of ≥6 ACH50. With these applicability constraints, this portion of the measure applies to about 92% of existing dwelling units. In total, portions or the full package apply to 92% of dwelling units. Not Applicable The insulation portion of this measure does not apply to dwelling units with: • Wood stud walls with existing insulation (any amount) • Non-wood stud walls. These constraints exclude about 70% of dwelling units from receiving wall insulation upgrades. The advanced air sealing portion of this measure does not apply to dwelling units with infiltration rates below 6 ACH50. This excludes about 8% of all dwelling units. The most common drill-and- fill insulation materials are cellulose, fiberglass, and spray foam. For cellulose and fiberglass, there are two main types of drill-and-fill installation: loose fill (also known as blown-in) and dense pack, which requires professional equipment (North 2012).
